name: multiple sclerosis overview
title: Multiple sclerosis: a relapse is new neurological dysfunction lasting 24 hours or more with no other cause; the typical relapses are myelitis, optic neuritis and brainstem or cerebellar syndromes; the diagnosis needs dissemination in space and time on MRI, with CSF oligoclonal bands able to stand in for time, once better explanations are ruled out; treatment is disease-modifying therapy by category plus symptomatic therapy

root.title: Could it be MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS (MS)?
lines: an immune attack (B and T cells) on central nervous system myelin → axonal damage, then loss
most common disabling neurological disease of young adults in Canada · women 3:1 · age 20-40
risk: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV, 32-fold) · adolescent obesity · smoking · low vitamin D or sunlight · shift work

groups.title: A RELAPSE: which kind?
lines: NEW neurological symptoms · acute or subacute onset · lasting 24 HOURS or more · no other cause · not a pseudo-relapse
other features: sensory disturbances · fatigue · Lhermitte's sign (an electric shock down the back on bending the neck)

head: h
Myelitis
spinal cord lesion · about 50% at onset

rows: MRI is central · lumbar puncture supports
2017 McDonald criteria: clinical attacks + MRI or CSF findings, combined
lesions in 2 or more typical regions:
• a NEW lesion on follow-up MRI
• OR enhancing + non-enhancing lesions at once
• CSF oligoclonal bands can stand in for time
ALWAYS rule out a better explanation
neuromyelitis optica (NMO) · myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein disease (MOGAD) · vascular · infection · metabolic (B12)
Course: relapsing-remitting (85% at onset) → secondary progressive · or primary progressive from the start
score disability on the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS, 0-10)
• standard orals: dimethyl fumarate, teriflunomide, fingolimod
• high efficacy: natalizumab, B-cell therapies (ocrelizumab, ofatumumab, rituximab)
